question: A student secured 300 marks out of a maximum of x marks in a test. If the same percentage score were applied to a test of 400 marks, he would have scored 200 marks. What were the maximum marks of the original test?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Same percentage ⇒ ratios equal

300/x = 200/400

Cross multiply: 300 × 400 = 200x

x = (300 × 400) / 200 = 600

**∴ Answer = 600**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Student scored 300 out of x, and equivalent score is 200 out of 400

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Marks obtained / Maximum marks) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Percentage in first test = (300 / x) × 100

⇒ Percentage in second test = (200 / 400) × 100

⇒ Since both percentages are equal:

⇒ 300 / x = 200 / 400

⇒ Cross multiply: 300 × 400 = 200x

⇒ 120000 = 200x

⇒ x = 120000 ÷ 200 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is 600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Formula

Percentage = (Obtained / Total) × 100

Equivalent Ratios

If percentages are equal, their fractions are equal.

Cross Multiplication

a/b = c/d ⇒ ad = bc

Quick Check

200/400 = 50%, so 300 must be 50% of x ⇒ x = 600
